anomalies.observed: The 3.3 V logic supply pins of both MCP2515 CAN controllers, both SC16IS752 UARTs and the VCC1 side of both isolated CAN transceivers sit on the unnamed net NET0073. That net also carries the 3.3 V pull-ups (R37, R47, R55, R70, R46, R97) and decoupling capacitors. NET0073 has no regulator or source pin, and it is not merged with the named +3V3 net, which holds only other 3.3 V pins.
anomalies.expected: The VDD/VCC pins of these ICs and the pull-up network should be on the +3V3 rail, which is sourced by the TLV1117 (U13) regulator output.
anomalies.impact: If NET0073 is not tied to the 3.3 V output, the CAN controllers, UARTs and isolated transceivers have no logic supply and the CAN and UART interfaces cannot work. Their reset and chip-select pull-ups would also float.

anomalies.observed: R93 is valued "24k", but its library description and MPN describe a 24 Ω part (FRC0805J240TSD, 24Ω 0805), and the 24k value is also in the SPICE deck.
anomalies.expected: The schematic value should match the 24 Ω part that is specified, or the part should be changed to a 24 kΩ resistor.

evidence.quote: (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: The bleed or balance resistance across the VOUTP/VOUTN rail differs by a factor of 1000 from the part that would be fitted, changing the loading and dissipation on that rail.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of the three status LEDs D24, D29 and D42 are connected only to each other on net /NET0072. That net has no supply or other connection. The cathodes drive current-limit resistors from the CM4 Ethernet and activity LED outputs.
anomalies.expected: The anodes of these LEDs should be tied to the +3V3 supply, as D31 is.
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet and activity indicators cannot light, because there is no supply path through their anodes.
